warrington.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Warrington
s1loc: Warrington Foodbank, in the Trussell network, handed out close to 8,000 parcels in a recent year, while Warrington Voluntary Action coordinates the Warrington Food Network of churches, charities and community groups. St Rocco's Hospice has cared for the town since 1985 from its Lockton Lane base in Bewsey, funding it through shops in Latchford, Orford and Stockton Heath. The Bread and Butter Thing runs an affordable food service from Latchford Community Hub at St Margaret's, with pantries and food clubs spread across the borough.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops along the high street and order kit through central buying accounts, while small community groups, the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, affordable food pantries and volunteer-run projects make do on a shoestring across Latchford, Orford, Bewsey and Stockton Heath. We are set up to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for everyone else.

slough.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Slough
s1loc: Slough Foodbank, an independent charity backed by local churches in the Trussell network, runs distribution centres at Slough Baptist Church on Windsor Road, Langley Free Church, St Andrew's in Cippenham and Britwell Community Centre. Thames Hospice, founded by parishioners of St Anthony's RC Church in Slough, provides palliative care across Berkshire, raising funds through its charity shops. Alongside them sit faith groups, mutual-aid networks and the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks that keep food moving to households in crisis.

Colne Valley Help offers food support across the valley, and Affordable Food Clubs and community pantries run through the week alongside the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks. Severn Hospice cares for the area from Apley, funding its work through charity shops including a Telford branch, with Donnington friends groups fundraising year round. Community pantries include the Maindee Food Pantry at Maindee Library and the Pill Millennium Centre pantry in Pillgwenlly, both cutting food waste while feeding households. St David's Hospice Care, based on Blackett Avenue, has given free care for over four decades, and the Gwent Association of Voluntary Organisations supports food banks and community groups with grants.

oxford.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Oxford
s1loc: Oxford Mutual Aid delivers food parcels across the city, while SOFEA, partnered with FareShare, redistributes hundreds of tonnes of surplus food a month and supplies pantries through the county. Oxford Food Hub, formerly Oxford Food Bank, moves surplus from wholesalers to charities, and the Rose Hill Community Larder makes good food affordable. Sobell House Hospice, founded in 1976 as one of the UK's earliest, cares for Oxfordshire, and Oxfordshire Community and Voluntary Action acts as the hub for the city's community groups.

poole.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Poole
s1loc: Poole Food Bank works in partnership with Faithworks Wessex, with its Jimmy's hub at St James' Church Centre in the town centre and satellites at St Clement's, St Gabriel's and Calvary Pentecostal churches. Community Fridges in Branksome and Rossmore libraries share surplus food, and the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks keep supplies moving. Lewis-Manning Hospice gives free palliative care to Poole and the surrounding towns, while Dorset Community Foundation has granted almost 14 million pounds to local causes since 2000.
